Only what this port measured or had to solve; the much larger hardware corpus for this phone is moWerk's sailfish-rag Mainline/ (read-only reference, see README). boot_chain.title: U-Boot's bootmenu can show a menu at every boot through the environment alone
boot_chain.general: On qcom phone builds, bootretry=1 ends an extlinux menu at once, since endtime is unset before bootcmd. bootmenu has its own loop: bootmenu N counts down, bootmenu -1 waits for a key. env import -t in preboot can load labels and the delay from a file on disk, so they change without a reflash.
boot_chain.instance: Pro¹x, U-Boot environment in packages/uboot.scm, labels from /boot/extlinux/menu.env. Author's test with -1: menu waits, keys work, a previous entry boots; with 15, the countdown worked and the default entry booted (author's test).

boot_chain.title: Qualcomm ABL rejects a U-Boot arm64 Image whose header text_offset is not zero
boot_chain.general: The Qualcomm Android bootloader (ABL) checks the arm64 Image header of the kernel in the boot image. A U-Boot binary built with a negative text_offset (bytes 8-15 of the header) is refused and the phone falls straight back to fastboot, with no message. Zero text_offset as Linux does, gzip the image, and append the DTB after the gzip stream so ABL hands it to U-Boot in x0.
boot_chain.instance: Pro¹x, U-Boot packed as an Android boot image in boot_a/boot_b by scripts/flash.sh. U-Boot's header had text_offset = -0x80000000. The NixOS port already did this; the Guix flash script had missed it. --second was dropped once the DTB was appended.

boot_chain.title: AVB vbmeta flags are at byte offset 120 of the header
boot_chain.general: To disable verification with a hand-made vbmeta image, the flags word (value 3: verification and hashtree disabled) goes at byte offset 120 of vbmeta_image_header_t, and the image is zero-padded to 4096 bytes. Writing it anywhere else leaves verification enabled, and ABL rejects the unsigned boot image by falling back to fastboot.
boot_chain.instance: scripts/flash.sh first wrote the flag at offset 48 (the signature_offset field). Fixed by building the header with Python struct.pack_into so the offset is explicit (scripts/mkvbmeta.py).

boot_chain.title: Flash U-Boot to both boot slots and set slot A active
boot_chain.general: On an A/B Qualcomm phone, if only one boot slot holds the new bootloader, a failed boot can make ABL switch to the other slot and boot the old stock image, or loop between slots. Flashing both slots avoids the loop, but it leaves no stock slot to fall back to: the only way back to Android is a reflash.
boot_chain.instance: scripts/flash.sh flashes boot_a, boot_b, vbmeta_a and vbmeta_b, erases dtbo, flashes userdata, then runs set_active a. The README still says 'replaces the bootloader on slot A' only (as of 018fa97).

boot_chain.title: A one-shot boot entry with a known-good default makes kernel experiments recoverable without hands
boot_chain.general: With U-Boot and extlinux, boot the system under test through a one-shot entry while the default stays a known-good system, so any crash or hang comes back to something reachable over ssh after a reset. Without it, a kernel or initrd that does not boot needs a person at the boot menu.
boot_chain.instance: moWerk's SailfishOS port keeps NixOS as the default on userdata and enters SailfishOS through a one-shot extlinux entry. This Guix port has no such mechanism yet: recovery is the volume-down boot menu with previous generations (TODO.md section 11).

boot_chain.title: U-Boot extlinux refuses kernel command lines over 511 bytes (CONFIG_SYS_CBSIZE=512 in qcom_defconfig)
boot_chain.general: U-Boot builds bootargs for an extlinux/PXE label in a CONFIG_SYS_CBSIZE buffer; a longer APPEND prints "bootarg overflow" and the label does not boot. qcom_defconfig sets 512. Long store paths (gnu.system, gnu.load) already take about half of it on Guix; options like vt.default_red/grn/blu push it over. Raise CONFIG_SYS_CBSIZE or keep the command line short.
boot_chain.instance: Pro¹x, U-Boot 2026.10-rc f8eb346: generations 22-24 with the three vt.default_* arguments (APPEND 569 bytes) did not boot; the phone came up from prev3 (generation 21, 284 bytes). The palette moved back to setvtrgb at boot. Generation 25: 317 bytes.
boot_chain.source: boot/pxe_utils.c label_boot (bootargs[CONFIG_SYS_CBSIZE]), configs/qcom_defconfig in the u-boot-pro1x source; /proc/cmdline on the phone (gnu.system=system-21-link); APPEND lengths in /boot/extlinux/prev*.conf

kernel.title: QRTR name service and PD mapper are in the kernel config; no userspace daemons needed for them
kernel.general: Recent kernels provide the QRTR name service and the protection domain mapper in-kernel (CONFIG_QRTR, CONFIG_QCOM_PD_MAPPER). Guides that list qrtr-ns and pd-mapper daemons are outdated. rmtfs and tqftpserv are still needed.
kernel.instance: CONFIG_QRTR=y and CONFIG_QCOM_PD_MAPPER=y in device/kernel/config.aarch64. rmtfs, tqftpserv and pro1x-hexagonrpcd run as Shepherd services (seen running on the 2026-10-27 flash, per TODO.md).

kernel.title: Enable zstd firmware decompression when the firmware package ships .zst files
kernel.general: If the distribution compresses firmware files, the kernel firmware loader needs the matching option (CONFIG_FW_LOADER_COMPRESS_ZSTD or _XZ), or every request_firmware fails as 'file not found' although the file is there.
kernel.instance: Enabled in device/kernel/config.aarch64 for the Guix build. The reason (linux-firmware from nonguix shipping .zst files) is not written in the commit.

kernel.title: s2idle: the Bluetooth UART wakes the SoC at once
kernel.general: On Qualcomm phones with a UART-attached Bluetooth chip, the UART RX wake IRQ can end every s2idle within seconds; disable that device's power/wakeup while suspended (Bluetooth keeps working).
kernel.instance: Pro1X, Linux 7.1 sm6115-mainline: woke after 2.2 s on IRQ 110 4a8c000.serial:wakeup (/sys/power/pm_wakeup_irq); with /sys/devices/platform/soc@0/4ac0000.geniqup/4a8c000.serial/power/wakeup disabled it slept until the power key (IRQ pm8941_pwrkey) or the RTC alarm (pm8xxx_rtc_alarm).
kernel.source: device/sway/pro1x-sleep; suspend tests on the phone 2026-11-01

kernel.title: s2idle: the ADSP sensor process crashes at resume (fastrpc resends the frozen listener call)
kernel.general: With hexagonrpcd serving the ADSP sensor PD, the freezer interrupts its listener ioctl (-ERESTARTSYS) and mainline fastrpc sends the restarted call again; the duplicate crashes sensor_process in frpc_dsp at resume. Stopping only the sensor clients does not help. Fix in the kernel: resume the interrupted context (downstream context_restore_interrupted) and take a wakeup event per DSP message.
kernel.instance: Pro1X 7.1: PDM: service sensor_process crash EX:sensor_process:0x1:frpc_dsp:0xc0 at every resume; ADSP recovery (debugfs recover) then brought sensors back but not the sound card (wcd937x_codec ASoC error -16, snd-sm8250 failed -16; the codec cannot be unbound: Permission denied), so no sound until reboot. Same crash and cause on the Lenovo TB-J606L (SM6115); its patches 0015/0016 carried as pro1x-fastrpc-wake / pro1x-fastrpc-resume-interrupted (0016 adapted to 7.1). postmarketOS google-sargo stops hexagonrpcd before suspend instead.
kernel.source: github.com/haltia-de/device-lenovo-tb-j606l issues/23, pull/12, kernel/patches; pmaports MR 5400; crash and audio loss confirmed on the Pro1X; the fix not yet booted

kernel.title: s2idle: modem messages do not wake user space (GLINK SMEM is IRQF_NO_SUSPEND without a wakeup event)
kernel.general: qcom_glink_smem requests its IRQ IRQF_NO_SUSPEND and reports no wakeup event, so an incoming call is received by the kernel in s2idle while ModemManager stays frozen. smp2p is wakeup-capable but off by default and carries no QMI messages.
kernel.instance: Pro1X 7.1, drivers/rpmsg/qcom_glink_smem.c line 308; our patch pro1x-glink-modem-wake takes a wakeup event on the mpss edge; /sys/devices/platform/smp2p-mpss/power/wakeup disabled. Kernel v3 (2026-11-01): wakeup only for QRTR data to user-space sockets (af_qrtr, sk_kern_sock false), switch /sys/module/qrtr/parameters/wake_on_data; v1 (every GLINK message) and v2 (every QRTR data packet) aborted each suspend: 2-4 packets of 48 bytes 0.2-0.4 s after each entry. With v3 an RTC-woken suspend held 45 s, woken by the RTC only, ADSP and sound intact. Wake on an incoming call not yet tested.
kernel.source: kernel source read; patch not yet booted

kernel.title: s2idle does not reach SoC deep sleep: qcom_stats vlow and vmin stay at 0
kernel.general: On SM6115 mainline, a held s2idle only idles the CPUs (psci per-core power collapse); the RPM low-power modes vlow/vmin need every master (modem, ADSP, CDSP, WCN) to vote for sleep and XO to be released. Check /sys/kernel/debug/qcom_stats/{vlow,vmin} Count before trusting a suspend drain figure.
kernel.instance: Pro1X 7.1: psci_idle driver, states WFI and cpu-sleep-0-0 / cpu-sleep-1-0 used; vlow and vmin Count 0 after suspends of 11 s and more (2026-11-01). moWerk measures 47.5 mA in suspend on SailfishOS (7.3) and suspects the same; the TB-J606L port (SM6115) reports vlow/vmin at 0 with XO votes as its next step.
kernel.source: qcom_stats and cpuidle sysfs on the phone; moWerk (message to the author); github.com/haltia-de/device-lenovo-tb-j606l pull/12

kernel.title: qx1000-linux-mainline: Linux 7.3.3 for the Pro1 (QX1000, MSM8998), a sibling of this phone
kernel.general: A mainline tree for a sibling device (same maker, same slider keyboard and panel, an older SoC) shares fixes for the common parts: panel, QRTR, keyboard, Wi-Fi chip family. Read its per-commit patches before solving those here, and keep its SoC-specific work (CPR, DisplayPort, PMI8998) for a port to that device.
kernel.instance: github.com/sampavlovic/qx1000-linux-mainline (Sam Pavlovic, with Giuseppe Maggio, AngeloGioacchino Del Regno, Teguh Sobirin, moWerk), read 2026-11-22 at 08894aac2: about 70 commits on Linux 7.3.3, one fix each, and qx1000/ with a build script and a systemd/Debian-style rootfs overlay (ALSA UCM for sdm845 Fxtec-Pro1, keyd and xkb layout, modprobe, udev, Wi-Fi board file and MAC helpers). kernel.title: Hibernation with the swap inside an offset LUKS container: the loop device's freezable workqueue hangs the image write; dm-linear does not
kernel.general: Kernel threads stay frozen while the hibernation image is written (hibernation_snapshot thaws them only on error). A block device served by a freezable worker, such as the loop driver (WQ_FREEZABLE), never completes the write, and the machine hangs at the first page. A device-mapper linear target remaps requests in place, without a thread, and keeps no second page cache of the disk.
kernel.instance: Pro¹x, LUKS2 at an offset inside userdata, swap file inside it. Previously on /dev/loop0 (losetup -o): hung at the first image write (2026-11-18). Replaced by /dev/mapper/pro1x-part made with DM ioctls by pro1x-dm-offset in the initrd (no udev, no dmsetup).
kernel.source: 0cc4983; see the storage_and_fde entry on losetup -o, which this replaces

kernel.title: Hibernation on SM6115: the SMP2P sleep-state driver's interrupts abort the freeze
kernel.general: The remote processors' sleep-state interrupts (qcom smp2p sleep state, raised by the ADSP's sensor traffic) are hard wakeups, so every hibernation aborts while the kernel threads freeze. Make the driver raise no wakeups during hibernation, or unload it first.
kernel.instance: Pro¹x, kernel patch of 7246bfa; before it, pro1x-sleep unloaded the driver (rmmod).
kernel.source: 7246bfa, 1cd7ee4 (TODO: the cause was the sleep-state driver alone)

kernel.title: Hibernation: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and the PMIC temperature alarm do not survive the power-off; unload them before the image
kernel.general: After a hibernation power-off, drivers whose firmware lives in a DSP restore against firmware that is gone. Here the restore waited 46 s for it, the PMIC temperature alarm's interrupt fired without end, and user space stalled before the DSPs were restarted. Unload them before writing the image, and load them again after the DSPs are up.
kernel.instance: Pro¹x, ath10k_snoc, the Bluetooth driver (hci_uart / btqca), spmi temp-alarm and its ADC users; unloaded and reloaded by pro1x-sleep. The unload and reload were tested without hibernation. Hibernation is offered no more (c5d2aa5): the session does not survive the DSPs' reset.

kernel.title: An Android container with CAP_BLOCK_SUSPEND blocks the host's sleep through EPOLLWAKEUP timers
kernel.general: The kernel honours EPOLLWAKEUP only for a process holding CAP_BLOCK_SUSPEND. An Android container that keeps this capability turns system_server's alarms into host wakeup sources, and every suspend or hibernation aborts at 'Freezing remaining freezable tasks aborted', with [timerfd] wakeup sources active. Drop block_suspend from the container's kept capabilities.
kernel.instance: Pro¹x, Waydroid's lxc.cap.keep; removed at boot by pro1x-waydroid-props and after waydroid init or upgrade by pro1x-waydroid-admin.

modem.title: ModemManager needs udev tags on rmnet_ipa0 to pair the IPA data port with the QRTR control port
modem.general: With ModemManager's qcom-soc plugin, the IPA network interface must carry ID_MM_CANDIDATE=1 and ID_MM_PHYSDEV_UID=qcom-soc, or MM never associates it with the modem found over QRTR and mobile data cannot come up. The IPA driver can register the interface before the rule is loaded, so re-trigger udev (udevadm trigger, settle) before starting MM. ModemManager ships these tags itself in 77-mm-qcom-soc.rules (DRIVERS==ipa or bam-dmux), so installing MM's udev rules is enough; a device rule is a fallback.
modem.instance: Image 6b37ac4, 2026-10-28: MM 1.24.0 probes qrtr0, then "couldn't create modem for device 'qcom-soc': Failed to find a net port in the QMI modem". udevadm info on rmnet_ipa0 showed no ID_MM_* property at all: neither device/udev/60-pro1x.rules nor MM's own 77-mm-qcom-soc.rules (which tags DRIVERS=="ipa" net ports with ID_MM_PHYSDEV_UID=qcom-soc) was loaded (see guix.json, udev extensions). The rule text is right; the Guix wiring was wrong. Fixed, not yet re-tested.

modem.title: Build ModemManager for QMI over QRTR only: MBIM is not needed on SoC modems
modem.general: Qualcomm SoC modems are reached over QRTR with QMI, not MBIM. If the distribution's libmbim is too old for a newer ModemManager, disable MBIM support rather than packaging a new libmbim.
modem.instance: modem-manager 1.24 built without MBIM (needs libmbim >= 1.32) and with the qcom-soc plugin forced on.

modem.title: A voice-centric modem setting can keep a phone off LTE without VoLTE
modem.general: 3GPP lets a voice-centric UE that cannot do voice on LTE (no IMS/VoLTE, no CSFB from the operator) leave E-UTRAN. On a mainline port without IMS, check the modem's usage preference before blaming bands or carrier profiles.
modem.instance: Pro1X: 4G allowed and preferred, every LTE band enabled, carrier profile ROW_Commercial (the only generic one of 25: Asian, Brazilian, Russian operators), yet UMTS only, 28% signal; another phone gets 5G at the same place. qmicli --nas-get-system-selection-preference: usage voice-centric, voice ps-preferred. Not tested: data-centric is stored in modem NV (modemst via rmtfs), author's decision pending. moWerk's notes: LTE registered on this phone with another operator.

modem.title: GNSS: LOC service present, but no NMEA
modem.general: A QMI LOC service on QRTR does not prove the GNSS engine works; check that NMEA indications arrive before writing a location stack.
modem.instance: Pro1X, 2026-10-30: QMI service 16 (LOC v2) on QRTR; ModemManager lists gps-raw, gps-nmea, agps-msa/msb. SUPL server and agps-msb fail ('Failed to receive indication'); gps-nmea enabled but 'couldn't setup required NMEA traces: Operation timed out'; qmicli --loc-follow-nmea for 75 s: nothing; 30+ min indoors: nothing. No port has GPS on this phone (NixOS README: untested; moWerk: not started).
modem.source: ModemManager log and qmicli on the phone

modem.title: QMI data bearers are multiplexed; a second context may still be refused by the network
modem.general: ModemManager on QMI/rmnet multiplexes bearers (qmapmux links), so two data contexts are possible on the modem side. Whether the network accepts a second PDP context on another APN is the operator's decision; 3GPP cause 33 (option unsubscribed) is the network refusing, not a modem fault. A second bearer without its own 3GPP profile can fail with 'call-already-present' (same profile slot). Snapshot the 3GPP profile list before adding one, and compare after deleting it.
modem.instance: Pro1X, 2026-10-30: data bearer on qmapmux0.0; a second bearer created qmapmux0.1 (mux id 2); with a dedicated profile (IPv4) the network answered cause 33. The profile was deleted and the list compared with the snapshot: identical. Earlier refusals came from a mistyped APN.
modem.source: ModemManager log and mmcli on the phone

modem.title: Check the operator's published APN before assuming a separate MMS APN
modem.general: Many operators carry MMS on the data APN (APN type default,mms). A separate MMS APN entered by mistake makes every MMS download fail; with the combined APN, mmsd-tng fetches over the data connection. Restart mmsd-tng after changing its settings so it processes its queue again.
modem.instance: Pro1X with the author's operator: combined APN; after correcting the MMS APN and a proxy port typo (89 for 80) the four waiting MMS downloaded at once.

modem.title: A missed call on LTE can coincide with a network rejection, and is not a kernel matter
modem.general: Before blaming a kernel for calls going to voicemail on LTE, match call events against ModemManager's rejections and radio type: the same kernel can ring on LTE minutes earlier. Repeated EMM rejections and detaches leave moments in which a call is lost.
modem.instance: Pro1x, Free SIM (208-15), 2026-11-05, kernel 7.3.0, generation 219: rang at 09:12:45 with LTE system info 7 s before and LTE after. At 09:13:51 a call appeared in ModemManager as unknown -> terminated in the same second as rejection 'ms-identity-not-derived-by-network' (9), 'no-cells-in-location-area' (15) and bearer end emm-detached. Causes 9 and 15 are logged on every day from 2026-10-30, with 7.1 too. This replaces the earlier notes' 'on 7.3 4G does not ring' and the QRTR lead, which had no evidence. Which of the author's call attempts is which event is not established; why the network rejects, and whether Android on this SIM behaves the same, is not known.
modem.confidence: confirmed (timings, one ring and one lost call), inferred (rejection causes the loss)
modem.source: /var/log/messages on the phone, ModemManager lines; author's test calls

modem.title: Incoming calls on LTE: about one in three rings, whatever the voice domain or a busy data link
modem.general: A phone without VoLTE on an LTE network receives calls by CS fallback: the network moves it to 2G/3G for the call. Count rings against calls with the caller reporting each result, and log the radio beside them. A voicemail with no radio change leaves no trace on the phone, so the phone cannot detect it. Poll the modem directly as well: ModemManager 1.24 logs 'unexpected LTE system info: domain camped' and reports searching and packet-detached while QMI serving system says registered, CS and PS attached.
modem.instance: Pro1X, 7.3.0, generations 229-232, SIM home 20815, 2026-11-05. Starting on Free LTE. Voice domain ps-preferred, no ping: rang 1 of 3 (first round), 2 of 5 (second round: 2 voicemails with no radio change, 1 with a move to 3G and no ring). cs-preferred, until power cycle: 2 of 5 by the author's count, 1 ring in ModemManager's log. ps-preferred with 49 pings/s on the data link: 1 of 3 (1 voicemail with no radio change, 1 with a move to 3G and no ring). Orange 20801 3G: 6 of 6 rang. Neither setting nor a busy link changed the result visibly, on small samples. Each ring came with a move to 3G. Reject cause 9 on PS and a dropped bearer follow most returns to LTE; a call rang 16 s after one, so it does not block calls by itself. Bouygues refuses the SIM with cause 11, SFR with 13. A return to LTE took from seconds to 10 min. 7.1 (#182), ps-preferred: 0 of 3 rang. cs-only, until power cycle: 0 of 3. Every voicemail in these two rounds left no trace on the phone. Carrier profile (PDC software): ROW_Commercial active; the 24 others are Asian, Brazilian, Russian; IMS QMI services answer InvalidOperation, so the modem's VoLTE capability cannot be read. Ping traffic: 2.5 kB/s measured on qmapmux0.0, about 9 MB/h.
modem.confidence: confirmed for the counts and logs; the cause is not known
modem.source: /root/call-test/net.log and cs.log on the phone, /var/log/messages, author's report per call

modem.title: VoLTE with 81voltd on SM6115: the modem opens its IMS bearer at once, and calls on LTE ring
modem.general: A Qualcomm modem that has its own IMS stack (QRTR services 33 IMS application, 18 IMS settings, 77 IMS priv) asks the host for the IMS data connection through the IMS Data service (770). Serve it with 81voltd: the modem chooses the APN and opens it through ModemManager. Where the network expects VoLTE on LTE, this is what makes incoming calls ring. After a stay on 3G the bearer closes and may not come back on LTE: restarting 81voltd reopens it. Outgoing calls may still fall back to CS.
modem.instance: Pro1X, 7.3.0, generations 233-236, SIM home Free 20815, carrier profile ROW_Commercial, 81voltd a7794dd, 2026-11-05. Bearer on APN ims, IPv6 only, within seconds of 81voltd's start (IPv4 refused: pdn-ipv4-call-disallowed). Incoming on LTE: 8 of 8 rang, 7 over VoLTE (no radio change), 1 by CS fallback; audio both ways in 7, one silent. Outgoing: 22-26 s dialing on LTE, then a move to Orange 3G and ringing within 1 s. After that, the IMS bearer was closed (regular-deactivation) and none came back on LTE; calls went to voicemail until 81voltd was restarted. pro1x-volte-watch: a bearer disconnected by hand was back 33 s later. Without 81voltd: about one in three rang (other entry).
modem.confidence: confirmed (calls by the author, logs on the phone)
modem.source: /var/log/messages, /var/log/81voltd.log, /var/log/pro1x-volte-watch.log, /root/call-test/net.log on the phone; author's report per call

usb_network.title: Keep the phone's DHCP server from handing the host a default route
usb_network.general: When the phone serves DHCP on the USB gadget interface, it must not advertise a router (DHCP option 3), or the host replaces its own default route with the phone and loses its network.
usb_network.instance: dnsmasq in usb-network.scm started with --dhcp-option=3 (empty), phone at 172.16.42.1.

usb_network.title: The USB controller is SuperSpeed-capable but runs at high speed on the PC cable; the built-in g_cdc can be unbound through the gadget bus to make room for a configfs gadget
usb_network.general: A precomposed gadget built into the kernel (CONFIG_USB_CDC_COMPOSITE=y) holds the only UDC, so no configfs gadget can bind; but since the gadget bus (Linux 5.19+) legacy gadget drivers are bus drivers with sysfs bind and unbind files, so `echo gadget.0 > /sys/bus/gadget/drivers/g_cdc/unbind' frees the UDC without a reboot or a kernel change, and `bind' puts it back. The replacement composite gadget keeps the same usb0 if its ECM function gets the same host_addr and dev_addr. Check the link speed before planning bandwidth: /sys/class/udc/*/current_speed against maximum_speed.
usb_network.instance: Pro1x, Linux 7.3.0, generation 283: /sys/class/udc/4e00000.usb maximum_speed super-speed, current_speed high-speed on the SSH cable to the PC (480 Mbit/s; isochronous at most 3 x 1024 bytes per microframe, about 24 MB/s); /sys/bus/gadget/drivers/g_cdc/ has bind, unbind and gadget.0; configfs (CONFIGFS_FS=y, USB_CONFIGFS=m, usb_f_ncm/ecm/acm/fs available) was not mounted. dmesg: g_cdc 'couldn't find an available UDC' at 0.87 s (dwc3 probe deferred), bound at 962 s; so g_cdc registers without match_existing_only and stays registered for a later bind. The unbind itself was not run (the cable was the live SSH link). Scripted in device/usb-video/pro1x-usb-gadget.
usb_network.confidence: confirmed (sysfs, dmesg, udc/core.c of 7.3); the unbind not yet run: inferred
usb_network.source: ssh root@172.16.42.1: /sys/class/udc, /sys/bus/gadget, zcat /proc/config.gz, dmesg; linux-7.3 drivers/usb/gadget/udc/core.c (gadget_bus_type, usb_gadget_register_driver_owner)

storage_and_fde.title: Passphrase prompt on the phone: console, keyboard and timing
storage_and_fde.general: A generation whose initrd tries small LUKS files on a plain root tests the prompt, keyboard and Argon2 cost without wiping anything. The initrd's static Guile has no ioctl symbol and no udev or losetup: find the partition through /sys/class/block/*/uevent PARTNAME and set up the loop with a small static program. cryptsetup 2.8 aborts on --tries 0.
storage_and_fde.instance: Pro¹x, generations 212-213: readable in landscape, letters and digits right without Fn, no echo; partition found at 2.4 s; Argon2id 256 MiB, 4 passes, unlock 8 s including typing 10 digits. Real layout on UFS not flashed yet.

storage_and_fde.title: cryptsetup cannot open LUKS2 at an offset; use a loop device with losetup -o
storage_and_fde.general: cryptsetup's --offset applies to plain and loop-AES mappings, not LUKS2. To place a LUKS2 container after an unencrypted region on the same partition, expose the region with losetup -o <bytes> and open LUKS2 on the loop device. The kernel needs CONFIG_BLK_DEV_LOOP=y if this happens in the initrd.
storage_and_fde.instance: userdata keeps a 256 MiB plain area (boot files for U-Boot) followed by LUKS2. fxtec-pro1x/services/fde.scm. FDE as a whole is untested on the device.

storage_and_fde.title: Grow the root filesystem to the partition on first boot by comparing sizes, not with a flag alone

wifi.title: WCN3990 (ath10k): an access point beside a 5 GHz client is refused (no IR while associated)
wifi.general: One radio allows AP+STA on a single channel, but while it is a client on 5 GHz every 5 GHz channel is flagged NO_IR in the wiphy, so no AP can start there; alone it can. cfg80211's CFG80211_REG_RELAX_NO_IR only lifts NO_IR for a P2P group owner (and station/TDLS), never for AP mode, and needs the driver's REGULATORY_ENABLE_RELAX_NO_IR and IR_CONCURRENT rules. On 2.4 GHz channels 1-11 AP+STA works.
wifi.instance: Pro1x, kernel 7.3, country FR applied (ath: regdomain 0x80fa, alpha2 FR; FR allows 5725-5875 without NO_IR). iw phy: 5180/5745/5765 MHz 'no IR' with wlan0 on channel 149, the flag gone 8 s after disconnecting, back on reconnect. ap0 AP on 149 stayed in config; ap0 on channel 11 beside a channel 11 client worked (2026-11-20). Kernel: CERTIFICATION_ONUS=y, REG_RELAX_NO_IR not set. Untested: a P2P GO (wpa_supplicant) instead of an AP, with REG_RELAX_NO_IR. 2026-11-24: with pro1x-ath-country-ie-no-ir, 5180 MHz is not 'no IR' while wlan0 is on 36 or 112, and ap0 starts beside it; and the radio allows two channels for AP+STA too (next entry).
wifi.confidence: confirmed (iw phy, NM log, chan.c read); why NO_IR while associated: not traced
wifi.source: /tmp/reg-test.log, /var/log/messages on the phone; linux-7.3 net/wireless/chan.c cfg80211_ir_permissive_chan

wifi.title: WCN3990 (ath10k): an access point beside a 5 GHz client carries data on another channel too (MCC)
wifi.general: The radio's second interface combination allows an AP beside a client on two channels (#{ managed } <= 2, #{ AP, P2P-GO } <= 1, #channels <= 2), not only on one. On the client's own 5 GHz channel the AP started (with NO_IR lifted) and devices got a lease, but no data passed, and after the client dropped the firmware failed to load the beacon ('bcn tmpl tx status' 2 or 3: dropped, filtered); an 80 MHz AP to match the client was worse (no beacon at all). On another channel the AP works, even beside a client on a radar channel where no AP may start, at the cost of latency: the radio alternates between the channels. A Wi-Fi Direct group owner instead of an AP is not usable under NetworkManager, which removes a group it did not start (RemoveInterface on wpa_supplicant's D-Bus), even with the P2P device unmanaged.
wifi.instance: Pro1x, kernel 7.3 with pro1x-ath-country-ie-no-ir, generation 259, firmware WLAN.HL.3.2.4-00982. Same channel: wlan0 on a third-party 5 GHz hotspot (36, 80 MHz), ap0 on 36 (20 MHz): laptop lease, 8 of 25 frames to it failed, reassociation every 30-60 s, no ping; tried once before a reboot, not retried on fresh firmware. Two channels: wlan0 on the home network (112, 80 MHz, radar), ap0 on 36: laptop pings 9.9.9.9 in 245-1135 ms through the home network; from the phone, 43-86 ms to 9.9.9.9 and 4-238 ms to the laptop, 1% frames failed. ap0 on 2.4 GHz channel 6 beside the same network: the laptop worked two minutes, then frames to it failed (183) and pings were lost; cause not found (2026-11-24). Corrected 2026-11-26: on the client's own channel it did carry data (SCC, ch 36 at 80 MHz, 3.5 Mbps to a laptop; entry below); the same-channel failure here, tried once, was not seen again.
wifi.confidence: confirmed (iw station dump, dmesg, D-Bus monitor, the author's laptop); same channel tried once; the 2.4 GHz stall not traced; the same-channel failure contradicted by the 2026-11-26 SCC test
wifi.source: dmesg, /var/log/messages and test logs on the phone (local); linux-7.3 ath10k wmi-tlv.c (beacon tx status)

wifi.title: WCN3990 (ath10k): 5 GHz AP beside a client needs the ath country-IE patch for non-DFS channels
wifi.general: One radio allows AP+STA on a single channel (SCC). Without a country, all 5 GHz channels are NO_IR while associated. With an EEPROM country (ath: 'Country alpha2 being used'), non-DFS channels (36-48, 149-165 in EU) lose NO_IR and an AP can start there on a secondary interface. DFS channels (52-144) keep NO_IR and radar detection: the firmware will not start an AP on them. The ath country-IE patch (pro1x-ath-country-ie-no-ir.patch) makes the driver accept a country from the AP's beacon when the card has an EEPROM country, extending this to foreign networks.
wifi.instance: Pro1x, kernel 7.3, country FR from EEPROM. Previously (2026-11-20): all 5 GHz NO_IR while associated, AP refused. With EEPROM country active (2026-11-26): channels 36-48 and 149-165 have no NO_IR, AP starts on ap0. DFS channels 52-144 still NO_IR. SCC confirmed on ch149 (a third-party hotspot) and ch48 (home router). The ath patch (pro1x-ath-country-ie-no-ir, running since generation 259) also takes the country from a foreign network's beacon.
wifi.source: iw phy on the phone, nmcli connection up pro1x-hotspot on ch149 and ch48; pro1x-ath-country-ie-no-ir.patch in device/kernel/patches/

wifi.title: WCN3990 single radio: SCC gives ~1/3 of station-only speed, MCC gives ~3 Mbps regardless
wifi.general: The WCN3990 has one radio. When the AP and client are on the same channel (SCC), the hotspot gets about a third of the station-only throughput. When they are on different channels (MCC), the radio time-multiplexes and both links drop to about 3 Mbps regardless of band or signal. Any two-channel operation triggers MCC: 5+2.4, different 5 GHz channels, or anything else. SCC is the only way to run a usable hotspot beside a Wi-Fi client.
wifi.instance: Pro1x, kernel 7.3. MCC (ch108+ch36, ch108+ch48, ch149+ch36): 1.8-3.5 Mbps on each link, 400-900ms gateway ping. SCC ch36/80 MHz (a third-party hotspot, -61 dBm): phone baseline 10 Mbps (one link), PC through hotspot (iperf3) 3.5 Mbps (two air hops on one radio, the radio alternates). LAN ping PC-to-phone on SCC: 20-330ms avg 142ms. 80 MHz confirmed on both interfaces initially, ap0 may drop to 20 MHz under load (firmware behavior). The two-hop relay (PC→ap0→phone→wlan0→external) is the fundamental bottleneck: expect about a third of the single-link speed. With a strong source (close 5G hotspot, -40 dBm) this should scale to 30-40 Mbps.
wifi.source: speed tests with curl proof.ovh.net through the hotspot; iw dev wlan0/ap0 info confirming same channel

wifi.title: WCN3990 (ath10k): a client's power save stays on when ap0 starts beside it, and cannot be turned on afterwards
wifi.general: The firmware has no multi-vif power save (fw_features lacks multi-vif-ps), so ath10k refuses to enable station power save while a second vdev (the AP) is started: 'refusing to enable ps on vdev 0: not supported by fw'. But starting the AP vdev does not re-evaluate the station's power save (ath10k_mac_vif_setup_ps returns early for non-station vifs, and mac80211 does not notify the station), so a station already in power save stays in it, in a state the firmware does not support, until the next power-save change on it. A hotspot beside a client must turn the client's power save off before (or right after) starting the AP, and keep it off; turning it back on while the AP runs is refused anyway. mac80211's own rule 'no PS with an AP vif' (ieee80211_recalc_ps) does not apply: ath10k sets SUPPORTS_DYNAMIC_PS, so PS is per-vif.
wifi.instance: Pro1x, kernel 7.3, firmware WLAN.HL.3.2.4-00982 (features wowlan,mgmt-tx-by-reference,non-bmi). ap0 started by NetworkManager on wlan0's channel (2.4 GHz, SCC) with wlan0 in power save: no kernel message, 'iw dev wlan0 get power_save' still on. 'iw dev wlan0 set power_save off' then 'on' while ap0 ran each logged the refusal (the 'off' too: ieee80211_set_power_mgmt calls hw_config(CHANGE_PS) before recalc_ps_vif, so the driver sees the old value once). Latency: in that stale state gateway pings from the phone averaged 122 ms (3-435) in one 20-ping run, 36 ms (2-133) after setting off; but the home 2.4 GHz link at -69 dBm was noisy that night (median 128-140 ms to the gateway with and without power save, no AP, 6 interleaved rounds), so the size of the effect is not established here; the 2026-11-19 stream measurement (640 ms average with power save on) stands. Until 2026-11-27 pro1x-hotspot left the client's power save as it was (on by default, NetworkManager wifi.powersave=3), so every Keep Wi-Fi hotspot ran in the stale state; now it holds it off (pro1x-wifi-powersave hold hotspot). Not measured yet with a device on the hotspot: scripts/hotspot-ab-test.sh. Also ruled out that night: CPU mode (pings over USB 0.75 ms in auto/battery at 1.3 GHz cap vs 0.97 ms in performance); the forwarding path (ip_forward on, NetworkManager's shared mode, mac80211 fq_codel TXQs on both interfaces, 13-47 kbit/s of background traffic).
wifi.confidence: confirmed (driver source and dmesg); the latency gain inferred, not measured

display.title: Ghost touches came from the panel running at 61 Hz: set the DSI pixel clock for exactly 60 Hz
display.general: A touch controller can pick up the display scan as touches when the panel refresh rate is off from what the stock firmware uses. Phantom touch events that appear only while the panel is on point at the display mode (pixel clock, porches), not at the touch driver. Compute the refresh rate as clock / (htotal * vtotal) and match the stock fps.
display.instance: BOE BF060Y8M-AJ0 panel (drivers/gpu/drm/panel/panel-boe-bf060y8m-aj0.c), 1236 x 2192 total. Mainline .clock = 165268 kHz gives 61.00 Hz and about 5000 phantom touch events per 10 s with the panel on; 162559 kHz gives 60.00 Hz and none. The fix is in device/kernel/patches/pro1x-dsi.patch, applied by fxtec-pro1x/packages/kernel.scm since the first commit 5ad022d. Arithmetic checked; not yet observed on this port with getevent/libinput.
display.source: nyymi (NixOS port author), message relayed by the author on 2026-10-28; device/kernel/patches/pro1x-dsi.patch lines 9-15

display.title: Reading the panel backlight (actual_brightness) wedges the DSI link; the panel fades to white
display.general: On a DSI panel whose backlight is controlled over DCS, reading actual_brightness makes the driver issue a DCS read (set max return packet size 0x37, then read). In video mode on this SoC that read times out; repeated polling (a status bar block) left the DSI host unable to send even writes, and the AMOLED panel slowly turned fully white. Power-cycling the output through the compositor did not recover it; a reboot did. Do not poll actual_brightness on such panels; reading brightness (the cached value) or writing it is the safe path, but check with dmesg.

Panel white; reboot needed. Block removed from device/sway/i3status-rust.toml.

display.title: BOE BF060Y8M-AJ0: sleep in sent from unprepare may never reach the panel
display.general: In a panel driver, DCS commands sent after the DSI host stopped video can fail; a void off() helper that drops accum_err hides it. Send them from disable while video still runs.
display.instance: The Pro1 has the same panel. On MSM8998 sleep in from unprepare timed out (wait for video done timed out, -ETIMEDOUT); qx1000-linux-mainline 8398dad56 sends it from disable, after display off, on top of moWerk's patch (our 0023). Here 0023 still sends sleep in from unprepare, through boe_bf060y8m_aj0_off(), which ignores the error: no timeout lines in /var/log/messages, but a failure would be silent. The regulators go off right after, so the effect is probably small. To confirm: log accum_err in off() once.

display.title: No DisplayPort over USB-C on SM6115: the SoC has no DP controller and a USB-only QMP PHY
display.general: DP Alt Mode needs three things in the SoC: a DisplayPort controller in the display subsystem, a USB/DP combo PHY, and a Type-C controller that enters the mode. Check the DPU catalog's interface list and the QMP PHY's compatible before planning it; a sibling device having DP (MSM8998 in the Pro1) says nothing about another SoC.
display.instance: Linux 7.3 dpu_6_3_sm6115.h lists one interface, INTF_1, type INTF_DSI (the panel); sm6115.dtsi has mdss_dsi0 only and usb_qmpphy is qcom,sm6115-qmp-usb3-phy (USB 3 only, no DP lanes). Snapdragon 662 is not sold with DP output either. So no kernel hack can add it. Options for an external screen over the port instead: a USB display adapter with a free driver (CONFIG_DRM_GUD: a Raspberry Pi Zero or Pico running the GUD gadget firmware as a USB-to-HDMI adapter, compressed frames over USB; CONFIG_DRM_UDL: old DisplayLink DL-1x5 USB 2.0 adapters). Both are off in config.aarch64. DisplayLink DL-3xxx/6xxx need the nonfree evdi userspace, not for this port. Wireless: Miracast/Chromecast (Network Displays) and wl-cast already work.

display.title: Adreno 610: 132 KB of tile memory makes multisampled render-to-texture passes cost hundreds of tiles; Godot 3D at seconds a frame
display.general: On a tiled GPU with a tiny GMEM every multisampled pass is cut into many more tiles, and the vertex work of every draw that touches a tile runs again per tile. GL_EXT_multisampled_render_to_texture is the cheap MSAA path on big-GMEM Adrenos but a cliff on the small ones. freedreno has no heuristic for it and its sysmem (bypass) path does not implement that extension at all, so FD_MESA_DEBUG=sysmem makes such a scene fast but empty. Hiding the extension (MESA_EXTENSION_OVERRIDE=-GL_EXT_multisampled_render_to_texture) makes engines that probe for it render without MSAA at full speed. Check the kernel's a6xx_catalog.c .gmem for the part before reasoning about tile counts.
display.instance: Pro¹x, Linux 7.3 (a610 .gmem = SZ_128K + SZ_4K), Waydroid LineageOS 20 image with Mesa 26.0.8 inside Android (the host's Mesa 26.0.2 only composes). Tesla app 4.62.x, Godot 3.2.2 GLES2 (upgrade_to_gles3 context), 4x MSAA via glFramebufferTexture2DMultisampleEXT. Logcat with FD_MESA_DEBUG=perf,msgs: Godot's 1048x1032 target at 4 samples; 111 frames in 64 s, mean 0.57 s, p90 1.1 s, max 11.2 s; GPU pinned at 950 MHz; no CPU stall or software fallback warnings. Android's hwui multisampled a 3816x2092 layer in the same process: 7920 bins of 32x32 a pass. With the extension hidden: Godot logs 'MSAA not supported on this hardware', 3147 frames in 73 s, median 16 ms, p90 42 ms, bins at most 49; same through Android properties only (mesa.extension.override, 3413 frames, median 16 ms). Screen was locked and off during the runs: the picture itself was not seen.

display.title: A dumb monitor (HDMI, DP, USB-C DP-only, XREAL glasses) cannot be fed from this port by software alone; the chains that can work
display.general: Displays that only take a video signal need either DP Alt Mode (absent on SM6115) or an adapter that turns USB data into HDMI or DP, with a driver on the phone. The GUD gadget side (samcday/gud-gadget, Rust over FunctionFS; the kernel f_gud_drm was never merged) runs on the display side, so it makes the phone a monitor for a computer, not the reverse; as a USB-to-HDMI adapter it needs a Linux board (Raspberry Pi Zero class) running it, with the phone as GUD host (CONFIG_DRM_GUD). Cheaper: a MacroSilicon MS912x USB-to-HDMI dongle with the free out-of-tree DRM driver (rhgndf/ms912x, GPL-2.0, branches per kernel including kernel-7.2; USB IDs 534d:6021, 534d:0821, 345f:9132, 345f:9133; resolutions limited, frames uncompressed, so USB 2 means low rates). Glasses like the XREAL Air take DP Alt Mode over USB-C only; XREAL's HDMI-to-USB-C adapter turns an HDMI source into that, and the XREAL Beam also receives Miracast, which this port already sends (gnome-network-displays). So for such glasses: phone > USB-to-HDMI dongle (driver) > HDMI-to-USB-C adapter > glasses, or phone > Miracast > Beam > glasses, with no cable to the phone.

CONFIG_DRM_GUD=m and CONFIG_DRM_UDL=m are in pro1x-7.3.fragment (not deployed yet). ms912x not packaged: it would be a linux-module-build-system package against linux-pro1x, built on CI. The author asked for both the UVC path and a dumb-monitor path on 2026-11-27.

video.title: gldownload's output is uncached memory: CPU reads per pixel are ~10x slower, and a Python buffer map copies the whole frame
video.general: On Adreno/Mesa, GStreamer's gldownload hands over buffers mapped from GPU memory without CPU caching. A block copy from them (the V4L2 encoder's input copy) costs a few ms, but any element or callback that reads them pixel by pixel collapses (videoflip after gldownload: 1.9 fps against 17.8 without). From Python, Gst.Buffer.map() copies the whole mapping into a Python object; use extract_dup(offset, size) for a few bytes. Every extra copy of a frame (e.g. pushing the same frame again to keep a steady rate) costs a full uncached read.
video.instance: Pro1x, Mesa freedreno A610, GStreamer 1.28.1. perf: 55% of the stream server in __memcpy_generic, in the encoder's input thread (queue0, 35%) and the GPU stage (20%). A per-frame Python map of the 1600x800 NV12 frame held the GPU stage at 6 of its 18 fps. Synthetic: upload+scale+turn+NV12 convert+download about 25 ms a frame, CPU conversion instead slower (8.9 fps vs 12.7).
video.source: scripts/stream-bench (phone-clock.py, stream-bench.py), PRO1X_STREAM_BENCH=1 in device/sway/pro1x-stream-webrtc; measured 2026-11-20 03:40-04:50

video.title: Repeated (damage-tracked) screen capture on swayfx 0.6 returns frames ~400-540 ms old; a one-shot grim capture is fresh
video.general: Measure capture age with a clock drawn on screen and decoded from the captured frames, at each stage. Here the portal's frames (xdg-desktop-portal-wlr 0.8.4, which prefers ext-image-copy-capture) were already ~400 ms old when pipewiresrc handed them over, at any frame rate (5-28/s), buffer count (2-8, min/max), or portal max-framerate; wf-recorder (wlr-screencopy with damage) read directly showed 544 ms (min 273), while grim's one-shot frames were drawn within +-30 ms. The GPU stage after it took 30-40 ms, the encoder 55-80 ms, network plus browser decode about 85 ms. Cause not found. Note: pipewiresrc hands buffers over oldest first, one per create(), with no skip to the newest. Later the same night: a leaky queue right after pipewiresrc (which drains its queue at once) left the portal's frames 457 ms old, so it is not a queue in GStreamer; PipeWire's graph is prompt (the portal's node drives a 21 ms cycle). Leading hypothesis (inferred, one sample): wlroots copies into the portal's DMA-BUF as an asynchronous GPU job (damaged region only, wlr_ext_image_copy_capture_v1.c copy_dmabuf) and sends ready at once; read before that job has run, the buffer still holds its previous frame, one turn of the portal's ring earlier (buffers/fps: 2 at 5/s and 8 at 20/s both predict 400 ms, measured 395 and 396). With a wait for the DMA-BUF's writer (poll POLLIN on its fd) the one frame that came was 195 ms old, then the portal sent no more.

video.title: Restarting the stream server (closing and reopening the portal capture and Venus) hard-hangs the phone at times (3 in 45 min)
video.general: Each start opens a ScreenCast session and the Venus encoder, each stop closes them. Cycled every minute or two, about 1 restart in 15 was followed within 30 s by a hard hang: nothing more in the log, no pstore record, and a watchdog reboot after 5-7 minutes. Matches the 2026-11-18 note that opening them per viewer powered the phone off. Avoid restart cycles; the server's own reexec (new size, rate or screen mode) goes through the same close and open. A third hang came at 05:02 while a server whose capture had stalled was running (its watchdog reopens the portal session after 75 s).

video.title: Repeating the last frame to keep the stream's rate steady tripled its delay on this phone
video.general: A clock that pushes the latest frame again when the screen sends none keeps the encoder's output even, but each push copies the frame again into the encoder. Where those copies are the bottleneck (uncached source memory), the real frames wait behind the repeats. Measured from a browser with the same settings: steady on 5.7 frames shown a second, 1.5 s old (key round trip 1.6 s); steady off 12 frames a second, 0.55 s old (95th percentile 0.69 s), key round trip 0.66 s, first frame 8 s after loading.

video.title: Venus (AR50 Lite) H.264 encoder: variable bitrate overshoots 4-7 times; constant bitrate about 2.5 times
video.general: Do not trust the encoder's rate control to hold the asked bitrate on a live stream. Measure what it sends, and set the bitrate when the encoder starts, not while it runs.
video.instance: Pro¹x, 1600x800, 20 fps, 2 Mbit/s asked: VBR sent 8-15 Mbit/s, the Wi-Fi backed up (1.7 s round trip, frames 2-10 s old); at 79 °C the heat limit held the encoder at 15 fps.

video.title: Screen to Venus with no CPU copy: wlr-screencopy into GPU buffers, rendered into the encoder's V4L2 buffers exported as DMA-BUFs
video.general: On this GPU, GStreamer's GL DMA-BUF export does not work, and the portal path's frames were 400 ms old before the encoder and cost over a core in copies. A small helper does it instead. The compositor copies the output into its GPU buffers. The GPU turns, scales and converts to NV12 straight into the encoder's input buffers (V4L2 EXPBUF, rendered as R8 and GR88 images). The encoder writes H.264 to stdout. This is how scrcpy works on Android.
video.instance: Pro¹x, pro1x-screencast: about 4% of a core, 32 ms median from Sway's frame to the encoded one at 20 fps. Sizes are rounded to multiples of 16, because a 1280x666 stream made the encoder pad 6 rows and a line flickered at the top edge (the cause is inferred).

video.title: Venus decoding with no GPU pass: GStreamer to GTK's DMA-BUF texture to Sway
video.general: A player that hands the decoder's DMA-BUFs to the compositor as they are, without drawing them on the GPU, plays 1080p for almost nothing. mpv's GPU output on the same clip costs most of a core.
video.instance: Pro¹x, a 1080p30 H.264 clip: Showtime about 2% CPU and a 582 MHz GPU average, mpv 65% and 944 MHz. Venus decodes H.264, HEVC and VP9.

video.title: The screen out of USB-C with no dongle: a UVC webcam gadget; Linux 7.3's f_uvc has frame-based H.264 and MJPEG, leaves the class requests to userspace, and caps a frame-based buffer at 460800 bytes
video.general: A SoC without DisplayPort can still show its screen on any computer through the port: the USB Video Class needs no driver or install on the host. The kernel gadget function (CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_F_UVC, usb_f_uvc.ko) exposes a V4L2 output device; userspace answers PROBE and COMMIT through UVC_EVENT_SETUP/DATA and UVCIOC_SEND_RESPONSE, then queues one frame per buffer (the FID toggles per buffer, EOF at its end). Formats come from configfs: streaming/uncompressed, streaming/mjpeg and streaming/framebased (frame-based, default GUID H.264, since the 2024 series; the host uvcvideo maps that GUID to V4L2_PIX_FMT_H264). Frame-based frames have no dwMaxVideoFrameBufferSize attribute, so the kernel's 460800-byte default sets sizeimage: keep H.264 keyframes under it or split an access unit over two buffers. The hardware encoder's H.264 stream can thus go to the host untouched; isochronous transfers do not retry, so repeat SPS/PPS and keep keyframes frequent. In a composite gadget, link the UVC function first so its interfaces are 0 and 1, which the userspace side assumes when telling control from streaming requests.
video.instance: Pro1x: config.aarch64 has USB_CONFIGFS=m, USB_CONFIGFS_F_FS=y, F_NCM/ECM/ACM/RNDIS, VIDEO_DEV=m, VIDEOBUF2_VMALLOC/DMA_SG=m, but USB_CONFIGFS_F_UVC off (added to device/kernel/pro1x-7.3.fragment, needs a CI build). Venus encoder /dev/video13 gives H264 and HEVC from NV12 (v4l2-ctl --list-formats); pro1x-screencast feeds it with no CPU copy (device/stream). ffmpeg on the phone has kmsgrab and an mjpeg encoder; gst jpegenc is absent. Prototype: device/usb-video (pro1x-usb-gadget, pro1x-uvc-feed, pro1x-usb-video); the feeder's parsing tested on the PC with ffmpeg streams, nothing run on the phone yet.
video.confidence: confirmed (kernel source 7.3: f_uvc.c, uvc_configfs.c, uvc_v4l2.c, uvc_video.c, drivers/media/common/uvc.c; phone sysfs); the gadget itself untested

keyboard.title: Keyboard backlight is an on/off GPIO LED; the slider is SW_KEYPAD_SLIDE on gpio-keys, 1 = slid out
keyboard.general: On sliders the keyboard backlight and the slide switch are separate devices: an LED class device and an EV_SW switch. Drive the LED from the switch and the panel state. The DRM connector sysfs dpms attribute follows the compositor output power (atomic ACTIVE) and is a cached value, so it is a safe panel-state source on DSI video-mode panels where backlight actual_brightness reads wedge the link.

audio.title: A sensor-stack crash on the ADSP takes audio down with it
audio.general: On Qualcomm SoCs the sensor core (SSC) and audio (q6afe/q6asm) share the ADSP. If the sensor core crashes during its init, the ADSP restarts and audio calls fail afterwards: AFE set params timeouts, the codec cannot get its clock, every PCM open fails with EBUSY. Check dmesg for 'fatal error received ... sensor_process' before debugging the audio stack.
audio.instance: Pro1X, Linux 7.1: 'fatal error received: err_qdi.c ... sensor_process ... SNS_REG_INIT ... sns_registry_sensor.c' at 12 s, then 'qcom-q6afe ... AFE set params failed -110', 'va_macro: unable to prepare mclk', wcd937x 'ASoC error (-16)', PipeWire only Dummy Output. Cause: hexagonrpcd da7a374 refused the sensor core's registry writes; 40e5041 accepts them and the crash is gone. SailfishOS's card re-probe (rmmod/modprobe snd_soc_sm8250) made it worse here: the card failed to instantiate until reboot.
audio.source: dmesg on the phone 2026-10-29; hexagonrpc source diff da7a374..40e5041 (apps_std_open_mode); commit 3305bd0

audio.title: The speaker amplifiers are fed by the codec's headphone stage: its gain sets speaker loudness
audio.general: On wcd937x boards with external speaker amplifiers driven from HPH, the HPH volume control decides how loud the speaker gets; a UCM default chosen for headphones leaves the speaker quiet even at 100% software volume.
audio.instance: Pro1X: HPHL/HPHR Volume 0..20 (higher is louder here, not inverted), UCM boot value 12. Author's listening test: 16 louder, 20 wanted for the speaker. Set to 20 in the Speaker devices of HiFi and Voice Call, 12 restored on disable so headphones and earpiece keep 12. The amixer dB scale shown for HPH (0.07 dB steps) is not meaningful.
audio.source: amixer on the phone; author 2026-10-29/30; commit 34eb12f

audio.title: S24_LE playback is about 40 dB too quiet on this card
audio.general: If a card plays far too quietly through the sound server but normally through aplay, compare the sample formats: the server may pick a format the codec path mishandles.
audio.instance: Pro1X: PipeWire opened hw:0,0 as S24_LE (hw_params); the NixOS port forces S16LE with a WirePlumber rule. Confirmed here: barely audible at full volume until the rule applied.

audio.title: Speaker amplifier switches found on with no session running; pops at login
audio.general: Pops when a sound server starts usually mean an amplifier is live while routes change. Read the amplifier switches while nothing plays before blaming the codec.
audio.instance: Pro1X, 2026-10-30: logged out, Spk0/Spk1 OUT Switch and HPHL Switch on although the Speaker DisableSequence ran (HPH gain back to 12). Spk0 went on again seconds after being switched off with no session running (cause unknown). At login PipeWire probes the Voice Call profile (VoiceMMode1 routes on/off for 0.6 s) and then enables HiFi Speaker; the author hears pops at login only. 'amixer events' lists 1279 controls for about a minute before reporting changes. moWerk reports pops at amp power changes, NixOS too.
audio.source: amixer cget/events on the phone; author 2026-10-30

audio.title: Login pops: the PipeWire probe opens the playback PCM repeatedly and each open powers the speaker amplifiers when their switches are left on
audio.general: On ASoC cards whose speaker amplifiers are DAPM widgets behind a mixer switch, a PCM open alone powers the whole path, amplifiers included, if the switch is on. WirePlumber/ACP opens and closes each PCM several times while it probes profiles at startup, so a switch left on by the previous session gives one amplifier power cycle per open: audible pops at every login. Turn the switches off before the audio daemon starts and let the UCM EnableSequence turn them on after the probe. Without ftrace, polling the DAPM debugfs widget files (/sys/kernel/debug/asoc/<card>/<component>/dapm/<widget>) every 10 ms together with /proc/asound/card*/pcm*/sub0/status gives a usable power timeline.
audio.instance: Pro1x, two aw87339 amplifiers (aw87339.1-0059/005a, widgets Spk0/Spk1 SPK PA) fed by the wcd937x HPH stage; controls Spk0/Spk1 OUT Switch. Restarting the Sway session PipeWire 1.6.8 + WirePlumber 0.5.17 by hand (generation 29): with the switches on, pcm0p opened about 8 times in 1.2 s and both amps plus HPHL/HPHR PGA were on from +0.57 s to +1.75 s, with one full off/on cycle. With both switches set to 0 first: 24 probe opens, amps never on; WirePlumber set the switches back on at +1.9 s (Speaker EnableSequence). Fix in pro1x-audio-session (amixer before pipewire). The kernel has no tracefs.
audio.source: DAPM/PCM logs /root/pops/082612 and the AMPS_OFF run on the phone; commit 2624e73, generation 30; the author no longer hears the pops (2026-10-30)

audio.title: A q6voice session does not survive its codec DMA port stopping
audio.general: The hostless voice PCM stays PREPARED, so another front end must keep the back end started. If that stream closes during a call (a card profile switch does), the other side stays silent even after the port and mixer are back; closing and reopening the voice PCM brings the sound back. Open the voice PCM after the keep-alive streams run.
audio.instance: Pro1x, 7.3.0, generations 216-217, 2026-11-04. #216: speaker on cut the sound, speaker off did not restore it, mixer identical. #217 restarts pro1x-voicepcm around the switch: earpiece, speaker and back all had sound both ways (author). The stopped port as the mechanism is inferred; the symptom and the cure are confirmed. The one silent call in #216 was the first after a boot, with pro1x-voicepcm powering the codec before the keep-alive stream; in #217's first call after a boot PipeWire did that and there was sound: two calls.
audio.source: device/audio/pro1x-voice-call; author's test calls; call-audio log

audio.title: Calls have no microphone processing on the phone: TX topology is NONE
audio.general: The q6voice driver's voice TX topology control decides whether the DSP runs echo and noise reduction on the uplink. VSS_IVOCPROC_TOPOLOGY_ID_NONE means none. Noise or echo behaviour heard on the far end then comes from outside the phone's DSP chain.
audio.instance: Pro1x, 7.3.0: 'VoiceMMode1 TX Topology' = 69488 (0x10F70, NONE), RX = 69495 (0x10F77, default). TX_SM_ECNS is 0x10F71, not tried; it may need calibration. Whether the modem processes the uplink further is not known. Tried on 2026-11-04, generation 218: TX topology set to TX_SM_ECNS (69489) by mixer before a call: no error, downlink fine, the far end heard nothing, in two calls; back on NONE the far end hears the phone. No calibration data exists in this port, the NixOS port or the SailfishOS port, and the driver has no way to send any; that this is why is inferred.

audio.title: Headphones stay 'availability unknown' unless the UCM device names its JackControl
audio.general: The codec's plug detection can already report the card's 'Headphone Jack' control while PipeWire keeps the speaker. Without JackControl in the UCM Headphones device, the port's availability is unknown, so priority alone decides. Name the jack, and give headphones a higher priority than the speaker.
audio.instance: Pro¹x HiFi verb: JackControl "Headphone Jack", priority 300 against the speaker's 200. Left out of the Voice Call verb, because a profile switch during a call needs the voice PCM restarted. alsaucm reads it on the phone; not yet tested with headphones plugged in.

sensors.title: SSC sensors need an SSC-enabled iio-sensor-proxy, not just hexagonrpcd
sensors.general: With the sensor core running (QRTR service 400), iio-sensor-proxy still exits if it was built without libssc; it finds no IIO sensor. Check the build option before the DSP side.
sensors.instance: Pro1X: iio-sensor-proxy 3.9 -Dssc-support=enabled with libssc 0.4.4; monitor-sensor: 'Has accelerometer (orientation: undefined, tilt: face-up)' lying flat. The firmware mount matrix is all zeros for every SSC sensor ('falling back to identity'); the udev ACCEL_MOUNT_MATRIX from the NixOS port applies to the accelerometer.
sensors.source: monitor-sensor and iio-sensor-proxy log on the phone; commit e4051eb

sensors.title: ADSP 'Handover signaled, but it already happened' repeats with every SSC sensor batch
sensors.general: On qcom PAS remoteprocs the handover SMP2P bit is meant to rise once at start; the q6v5 driver logs an error for each later rising edge. A streaming sensor client on an SSC (sensors on the ADSP) makes the ADSP raise its ready and handover bits again with each batch, so a running accelerometer stream floods the kernel log; count the smp2p and q6v5 lines in /proc/interrupts over 10 s with and without the client before suspecting a crash.
sensors.instance: Pro1x, kernel 7.1.0 (sm6115-mainline 8cd9520d), generation 33: smp2p-adsp, q6v5 ready and q6v5 handover 43-44 per 10 s with monitor-sensor --accel (iio-sensor-proxy 3.9, libssc) running, 0 without; wdog and fatal 0; ADSP stays up and audio keeps working. Started at the first login, when sway-autorotate started monitor-sensor.
sensors.source: /proc/interrupts on the phone; drivers/remoteproc/qcom_q6v5.c q6v5_handover_interrupt; arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/sm6115.dtsi remoteproc@a400000 interrupts

camera.title: IMX582 exposure capped at one frame of the minimum blanking: libcamera's simple pipeline never raises VBLANK
camera.general: With the software ISP (simple pipeline), libcamera takes the exposure range from the sensor's V4L2 controls at configure time and never writes V4L2_CID_VBLANK, so the longest exposure is the mode's minimum frame length. Dark scenes and indoor photos come out underexposed whatever the AE or a manual exposure asks. Pipelines that handle this (Raspberry Pi, rkisp1) raise VBLANK with the exposure.
camera.instance: Pro1x, IMX582 1984x1080 mode (pro1x-imx582-1080p), kernel 7.1 (3nfp9v97), libcamera-pro1x 0.7.2, 2026-11-02: subdev /dev/v4l-subdev19, vertical_blanking min 70 max 64420 (default and in use 70), hblank 1056, pixel rate 321.6 MHz, so 9.45 us a line; exposure max 1102 lines = 10416 us. Asked 30000 and 100000 us (manual) or auto in the dark: applied 10416 us every time (auto: gain 16, mean 0.2/255). Setting vertical_blanking=2120 by hand raises the sensor's exposure max to 3000-3152 lines, kept during streaming, but libcamera still applied 1102 lines. Up to ~0.6 s would be possible at the maximum blanking. Fixed by our libcamera patch 0018 (VBLANK raised per frame, priority delayed control): applied exposures 29993, 99991, 299992 us for 30, 100, 300 ms asked; 0.9 s asked gives 618700 us (blanking maximum, 65452 lines); 8 frames at 300 ms took 2.1 s; auto now up to 6982 lines (66 ms). Tested on the phone with the patched libcamera, not yet deployed.
camera.source: headless libcamerasrc test (agent's camtest.py through the camera app's environment), v4l2-ctl on the subdev; libcamera src/ipa/simple/soft_simple.cpp configure() takes exposureMax from configInfo.sensorControls

camera.title: A flash LED in the sensor's flash-leds, without V4L2 flash support, can leave a camera without media links
camera.general: When a device tree links a flash LED to a sensor, camss's async notifier may wait for a V4L2 flash subdevice. Without the kernel option that subdevice never registers. Check for 0 links in media-ctl first, then compare the config with a working port.
camera.instance: Pro1x, 7.3.0, patch 0027 flash-leds on the rear camera; imx582 and s5k4h7 present with 0 links, libcamera reports no camera, CONFIG_V4L2_FLASH_LED_CLASS not set although LEDS_CLASS_FLASH and LEDS_QCOM_FLASH are =m. moWerk's sfos.fragment sets it =m; it was the only camera-related difference found between his fragment and our config. Booted 2026-11-04 (generation 210): both sensors have links, white:flash-0 and dw9800 are entities, cam -l lists back and front, and the author reports the camera app more or less works. The notifier wait itself was not traced.
camera.confidence: confirmed that the option fixes it; mechanism inferred
camera.source: media-ctl and cam -l on the phone; moWerk kernel/sfos.fragment:70 and HANDOVER.md; device/kernel/pro1x-7.3.fragment

camera.title: libcamerasrc copies every frame whose row stride is not the tight width; GPU output rows are padded to 256 bytes
camera.general: libcamerasrc compares libcamera's stream stride with the stride GStreamer computes for the caps; when they differ and downstream does not accept video meta, it copies each frame with the CPU into a pool of its own. Reading GPU-written (uncached) dma-buf memory is slow: pick widths whose rows need no padding, or make downstream accept GstVideoMeta.
camera.instance: Pro¹x, libcamera 0.7.2 software ISP (GPU debayer): 48 MP at 7984 wide (rows 31936 bytes) was copied, 2.3 s per 190 MB frame ("Downstream doesn't support video meta, need to copy frame"); 7936 wide (rows of 31 KiB) is not, first frame 4.6 s after the switch instead of 8, then one every 0.6 s. 3968 (12 MP) was never copied.
camera.source: src/gstreamer/gstlibcamerasrc.cpp gst_libcamera_src_negotiate/gst_libcamera_create_video_pool; GST_DEBUG=libcamerasrc:5 on the phone; commit e2a9955

camera.title: The simple pipeline gives a raw stream beside the processed one, from the same sensor mode: photos without a mode switch
camera.general: With the software ISP the simple pipeline handler exposes two streams, processed and raw. Asking for a raw stream of the full sensor size makes libcamera pick that mode for both, the processed one scaled by the GPU debayer: the viewfinder runs from the photo's mode and the newest raw frame is the photo, developed outside libcamera with the frame's ColourGains and ColourCorrectionMatrix metadata. libcamerasrc needs caps names for the CSI-2 packed Bayer formats to offer such a pad.
camera.instance: Pro¹x IMX582: viewfinder 1472x1104 plus raw 4000x3000 rggb10p (stride 5000), both 17 fps in a dark room, 68% of one core; raw frame taken 0.02 s after the shutter, developed (Malvar-He-Cutler, 8 threads, JPEG q98) in about 1.1 s; colours match the viewfinder. Front S5K4H7: raw 3264x2448 grbg10p, stride 4080. Patch 0024 names bggr10p...rggb10p.
camera.source: device/camera/pro1x-develop.c, device/libcamera/af/0024-*.patch, commit e2a9955; headless tests and the app on the phone

camera.title: Rear camera module EEPROM: CCI bus 2 at 0x50, 8 KB, readable only while the sensor is powered, 8 bytes per transfer
camera.general: Qualcomm camera modules keep per-unit calibration in an EEPROM on the sensor's CCI bus, powered by the sensor's supplies. The CCI controller rejects long reads (16 bytes: EOPNOTSUPP), so read in small chunks, with the camera streaming or the supplies on.
camera.instance: Pro¹x IMX582 module: i2c-2 0x50 (0x51-0x57 absent), 16-bit addresses, wraps at 8 KB, 0x000-0xcbf used. 0x00 header (01 69 57 01 01 16 03 18), 0x10 AWB ratios, 0x21 lens shading 17x13 x 4 channels, 16-bit big-endian, 1023 at the centre and 211-287 in the corners (about two stops of vignetting), 0x70f AF calibration, 0x71f PDAF data. No QSC table (no room). The stock vendor sensor module file names an EEPROM driver and eepromSlaveAddress. The S5K4H7 (bus 3) not checked.
camera.source: i2ctransfer -y 2 w2@0x50 HI LO r8 while libcamera streamed; dump kept locally, not in git

camera.title: libcamera's soft AGC histogram is of raw values, before white balance: count clipping from the white point after the gains
camera.general: The software ISP's luminance histogram is computed from the raw Bayer samples. With large white balance gains (red about 4 under tungsten) the output clips long before the raw top bin, so a highlight limit on the top bin alone never triggers.
camera.instance: Pro¹x, patch 0023 (second version): a white area clips at raw luminance 0.299/gR + 0.587 + 0.114/gB of the range (0.76 with gains 4 and 1.16); samples from that bin up count. Compiled, deployed in generation 58; not yet seen on a bright scene.

camera.title: A pipeline's buffer count chosen at validation can stick from an earlier, larger configuration
camera.general: libcamera's gstreamer element validates the camera's default configuration (the largest size) before its negotiated one, on the same configuration object. A pipeline handler that fills bufferCount only when it is 0 keeps the first value: a count lowered for big frames then applies to small ones. With a raw stream whose buffers the app's queue and appsink hold, two buffers stall both streams after one frame (no error).
camera.instance: Pro¹x, libcamera 0.7.2 simple pipeline with our patch 0025 (2 buffers over 24 MP): rear 1472x1104 + 4000x3000 raw got 2 buffers from the 8000x6000 default; view and raw 0 fps, white balance stuck at the first frame (green photos). Fix: remember the counts validate() chose and recompute them. After: 15-19 fps both cameras.
camera.source: d3e884f; libcamera debug log (Adjusting bufferCount from 0 to 2 at the 48 MP validation)

camera.title: The IMX582 module EEPROM's lens shading table is interleaved per grid point
camera.general: Qualcomm-style module OTP lens shading tables (17x13) store R, Gr, Gb, B for each point in turn, 16-bit, with the brightest point (the centre) at 1023; the gain is 1023/value. Reading them as four planes gives nonsense (corners above the centre).
camera.instance: Pro¹x rear module, EEPROM at 0x50 on CCI bus 2, table at 0x21 (884 values, big-endian): corners R 211-231, G 259-279, B 272-287. Applied after demosaic with bilinear interpolation over the whole array: corners brighter, a pink centre cast gone, no extra time (1.1 s for 12 MP). The EEPROM answered with the camera off.
camera.source: 2e4d76d; dump read with i2ctransfer (kept out of git)

haptics.title: AW86224: the stock waveform file holds plain sine bursts
haptics.general: Before seeking a vendor's haptic blob, decode it: this one is a table of start and end addresses and full-amplitude sines, which a free driver can generate. The vendor's sharper feel likely comes from playing from chip memory rather than continuous drive.
haptics.instance: aw8622x_haptic.bin (1222 bytes, TheMuppets vendor repo): 2-byte checksum, base address 0, version 0x55, waves of 330, 809 and 59 samples, 60 samples per cycle (200 Hz at the driver's 12 kHz). LineageOS aw8622x.c uses wave 2 for short effects, a looped long wave otherwise. Not tried on the phone yet.
haptics.confidence: confirmed for the file and driver source; the feel is inferred

haptics.title: PMI632 LPG with ledtrig-pattern: hw_pattern is refused (EINVAL) until repeat is written
haptics.general: On activation, ledtrig-pattern shows repeat as -1 but keeps its count at 0. The LPG's hardware pattern accepts only -1 or 1, so every hw_pattern write fails until -1 is written to repeat.
haptics.instance: Pro¹x notification LED, pro1x-sleep's hibernation pattern: refused 4 times without the repeat write, accepted with it.

fingerprint.title: The fingerprint reader is a MicroArray sensor run by a QSEE trusted app; the SPI belongs to TrustZone
fingerprint.general: Many Qualcomm phones run the fingerprint sensor in TEE mode: the kernel driver only powers the sensor and forwards its IRQ, while image capture and matching run in a QSEE trusted app that owns the SPI bus. Such sensors cannot be read from Linux over SPI; a mainline port must load the vendor TA and speak its proprietary command protocol, or have no fingerprint.
fingerprint.instance: Pro¹x: vendor driver drivers/input/fingerprint/madev.c + qcom-settings.c (MicroArray v4.0.05, GPL, built with #define TEE and USE_PLATFORM_DRIVE: platform driver, no spi child), char device /dev/madev0, DT node microarray_fp (compatible microarray,fingerprint; reset tlmm 104, irq tlmm 97, power tlmm 108, suben tlmm 67). TA: vendor/firmware/mafp.mdt-style split mafp.mbn + mafp.b00..b06. HAL: microarray.fingerprint.default.so + libfprint-x64.so over libQSEEComAPI (qseecomd). Halium ports work because they keep the vendor kernel, qseecomd and this HAL.
fingerprint.source: LineageOS android_device_fxtec_pro1x (proprietary-files.txt, sepolicy/vendor/file_contexts) and android_kernel_fxtec_sm6115 (drivers/input/fingerprint, arch/arm64/boot/dts/vendor/qcom/bengal-idp.dtsi), read 2026-11-06

fingerprint.title: Mainline qcom_scm finds QSEECOM on this TrustZone but skips it (machine not allowlisted)
fingerprint.general: Mainline qcom_scm probes QSEECOM and only creates the qcom_qseecom device on allowlisted machines. The mainline interface only looks up TAs that firmware already loaded (qcom_scm_qseecom_app_get_id) and sends commands to them from kernel clients; it has no app loading and no userspace interface. Loading a vendor TA needs an extra (out-of-tree) loader. The newer QTEE driver (drivers/tee/qcomtee, smcinvoke) is only promised from SM8650 on.

nfc.title: nxp-nci: unbinding the driver hangs in nci_unregister_device when the chip stops answering I2C
nfc.general: Removing nxp-nci_i2c (an unbind through sysfs, or rmmod) hangs in D state inside nci_unregister_device. The cause is in the driver: nxp_nci_remove switches the chip to cold mode (enable pin low) before nci_unregister_device, which still sends a command to the powered-off chip. The I2C send fails (-6), the request times out, and the removal then waits forever. The device stays half removed: i2c-dev reports the address busy, and only a reboot clears it. A normal reboot may block on the same device lock, so sync and reboot with sysrq. To talk to the chip from user space, keep the driver from loading with module_blacklist=nxp_nci_i2c on the kernel command line. A file in /etc/modprobe.d is not enough: on Guix, udev's libkmod reads /run/modprobe.d (emptied at boot), not /etc/modprobe.d.

nfc.title: PN557 on the Pro¹x keeps Android's NXP settings in its own memory, and still finds no tag when polled by hand
nfc.general: NXP controllers keep the proprietary settings the Android HAL sends (clock selection, TVDD power, RF field notifications) across power cycles. Before sending them from Linux, read them with CORE_GET_CONFIG (extended IDs A0 xx) after CORE_RESET (keep configuration) and CORE_INIT. Polling by hand over i2c-dev, with no kernel driver, tells the chip and antenna apart from the kernel and neard. The chip NACKs the first I2C write after an idle period while it wakes from standby, so retry each write once.
nfc.instance: Generation 260 (module_blacklist=nxp_nci_i2c), VEN set by gpioset. CORE_RESET NTF: NCI 2.0, hardware 0x41, firmware 12.01.16. A0 0D answered status 09. 2F 02 00 (proprietary extensions) answered 00 00 01 5E 64. RF_DISCOVER for poll A, B, F and V was accepted (status 00). Over 50 s with a card on the back, the chip sent nothing: no tag, no PLL-unlock or TX-LDO error. GPIO 86 (CLKREQ) stayed low throughout (sampled every 10 ms), as expected with the crystal. A listen-mode discovery (A, B, F) with another phone reading at the back sent nothing either, though no listen routing was set. Neither the NixOS port, the SailfishOS port nor sailfish-rag has anything on NFC (2026-11-23). Other mainline Qualcomm phones with PN553 (sdm845 OnePlus, SHIFT6mq, Nothing Phone 1) name no clock in their nfc@28 node. 2026-11-24, generation 260 with nxp-nci and neard. As reader for 120 s, it found neither a card that a Flipper Zero reads nor the Flipper emulating that card; nor did a Flipper reading at the back find the phone in neard's Target mode. Then Android's settings were sent by hand over i2c-dev (i2ctransfer -f, the driver bound): NXP_ACT_PROP_EXTN, EXT_TVDD_CFG_1, RF_CONF_BLK_1 to 3, CORE_CONF_EXTN, CORE_CONF, CORE_RF_FIELD; one answer each. With CORE_CONF's RF_FIELD_INFO on, the Flipper reading at the back gave 126 RF_FIELD_INFO notifications in 11 s (the kernel logs "unknown ntf opcode 0x107"): the antenna and the receive side work. As reader, still no card, before and after an adapter reset (nfctool -0, -1). Whether the chip sends a field at all is not known. Vendor nq@28 names no regulator, nq-nci.c powers nothing but VEN, and the PCA9534 at 0x21 drives only the caps LED and the fingerprint power. Antenna self-test by hand, generation 262 (module_blacklist=nxp_nci_i2c), with the NXP HAL's sequences (AOSP hardware/nxp/nfc pn8x/halimpl/self-test): after 2F 02 00 and 2F 00 01 00, the TX LDO current measurement (2F 3D 02 01 80) answered 00 00 00 00 (raw 0 in the 50-100 mA range) with the field off, after the field-on command (2F 3D 02 20 01, answered 00 AA BB CC DD), 5 s later, and off again. AGC (2F 3D 04 02 C8 60 03) answered 0x006D, once 0x0059, with or without the field. So the transmitter draws no measurable current: no field is sent. Its supply (VUP, the TX LDO's input) or the antenna's connection is the next suspect. Then three times (generations 262 and 263, nxp-nci not loaded), sending Android's RF register blocks by hand stopped the whole phone at once, with nothing in the kernel log: once during the run that sent RF_CONF_BLK_1 (A0 0D, 243 bytes) right after EXT_TVDD_CFG_1, once at that same point, and once, step by step, the instant RF_CONF_BLK_3 (A0 0B, 94 bytes) was written, after CORE_RESET (reset config), CORE_INIT, 2F 02 00, EXT_TVDD_CFG_1 and RF_CONF_BLK_2 had all answered OK and the phone ran 16 s after the TVDD setting. The last time the phone was found off, and booted again by itself: PM6125 PON_REASON1 (0x808) read 0x03, hard reset and SMPL (sudden momentary power loss, in the downstream qpnp-power-on names), not the power key; FAULT_REASON2 (0x8C9) 0x10, S3_RESET_REASON (0x8CA) 0x80 (not decoded). The same blocks sent at 16:59 with the driver bound did not; whether the chip applied them then is not known (only the interrupt count was seen). RF_CONF_BLK_3 (A0 0B, one 87-byte value) then went through too, on the charger (+0.8 A), with VPH_PWR flat at 10 Hz. A network drop 41 s later was the phone's Wi-Fi roaming, not a power cut (uptime unbroken). With every stock setting in the chip: no tag in two 40 s polls with a card on the back, and the TX LDO measurement still 0. Android's firmware file (libpn557_fw.so) is 01.16, as in the chip; the vendor partition has no NFC power setting (init only sets /dev/nq-nci permissions), and the NXP HAL writes TVDD and the RF blocks only when its config changed or after a firmware download. nfc.title: NFC card emulation (badge replay) on mainline: no HCE in the kernel, but a UID-only badge can be presented via a raw NCI listen-A path
nfc.general: The mainline Linux NCI core has no host card-emulation (ISO-DEP listen / HCE) path: net/nfc/nci/ntf.c calls nfc_tm_activated only for NFC-DEP, and an ISO-DEP listen activation returns NCI_STATUS_RF_PROTOCOL_ERROR. The NFC netlink API also exposes no way to set LA_NFCID1. So neard/the core cannot emulate a card. But a reader that checks only the UID is satisfied during the ISO 14443-3 anticollision, which the controller answers autonomously from its Listen-A config before any higher-layer protocol. Presenting a chosen UID therefore needs only: CORE_SET_CONFIG with LA_NFCID1 (0x33) + LA_SEL_INFO (0x32) + LA_BIT_FRAME_SDD (0x30) + LA_PLATFORM_CONFIG (0x31), then one RF_DISCOVER entry with tech/mode NCI_NFC_A_PASSIVE_LISTEN_MODE (0x80), then RF_DEACTIVATE to stop. Since the driver holds the I2C bus, user space cannot do this over i2c-dev; the only route is a driver hook (vendor cmd or a sysfs raw-NCI node). A PN557 under NCI 2.0 rejects a whole RF_DISCOVER that lists the RFU active modes 0x05/0x85, so emit only the modes you need (moWerk). Crypto readers (DESFire, Mifare Classic with keys) are not fooled: only the UID is answered.
nfc.instance: Pro¹x PN557, linux-pro1x 7.3. Param IDs confirmed from the stock HAL capture (moWerk nfcd-nxp-i2c-plugin, config/nxp-i2c-init.hex): 30 01 08, 31 01 03, 32 01 60, 33 04 01 02 03 04. Implemented as pro1x-nfc-replay.patch (sysfs nci_cmd on the nxp-nci i2c device -> nci_core_cmd, the init-cmds path) plus pro1x-nfc-listen (builds the sequence) and replay_badge() in pro1x-nfc. Build-tested only: the listen sequence is NOT verified on the device, and whether the PN557 presents a custom NFCID1 in listen mode is unconfirmed on any port (moWerk have no card-emulation captured).
